title: Opening: Monday. Out in town, the job site
notes: Scene Book, Opening: Monday, section 5. Approved by Jim, Nov 21, 2026. Ray's lines, the two answers and their records are the Scene Book's.
On time means on site by 7:00. JIM: the Scene Book's shift starts at 7; arriving at 7:00 exactly counts as on time.
The Scene Book says the shift "plays out in a few lines" and gives these two. They are used as written.
"On site at 7:12 a.m." style records and "Worked the shift." are Claude's: the Scene Book says the game records whether you show up, honestly, without giving the line.

text: Ray says "Morning" without looking up. Nobody notices you were on time. In a small town, that's a kind of news too.

effects.title: Second Time This Week
effects.objective: Ray noticed. What do you tell him?

text: Ray doesn't look up from his clipboard. "Second time this week."

choices.label: "Traffic on [Route 46]."
result: Ray writes something down. He's heard that one.

choices.label: "That's on me. It won't be a pattern."
result: Ray looks up for the first time. "Okay." That's all. It's more than you got from him last month.
choices.record: Owned being late. Promise made: on time.
effects: proof:ownership:Owned being late to Ray. Promise made: on time.

effects.objective: You owned it. Promise made: on time.

text: You're good at the parts of this job nobody sees.
At 3:30 the town opens back up: the diner, the gym, the park, the church, and at 4 o'clock, the bar.
